summary: Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has served as a professor at Geumgang University and was attested as a professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2013.

Jørn Borup (1966–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University (~1999–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as associate professor (~2006–2023).

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg (PhD ~1992–1996 under Michael Hahn, also studying under Alexis Sanderson). He worked at Halle-Wittenberg (~1999–2006) and became a professor at the University of Marburg in 2007.
Jürgen Neuß is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn is a historian and philosopher who earned his PhD from the Technical University of Berlin in 1987. He served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and the MPI of Geoanthropology (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri (1892–1975) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (~1929–1947), later holding posts at Annamalai and Mysore.

K. A. Subramania Iyer (1896–1980) was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett. He served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (1921–1960).
K. Ammini Amma is an Indology scholar who conducted research at the University of Madras, where she is attested as a research student in 1940 and 1971.

K. Balasubramania Iyer (1892–1970) was an Indology scholar who served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and was attested as Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute in 1945.
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from ~1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai (1902–1968) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Hartley College and studied at the University of London from ~1933 to 1936.

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) was an Indologist and linguist who earned PhDs from the University of Madras (under C. Kunhan Raja) and the University of London (under John Brough). In 1951, he became Professor and Head of Sanskrit at Madras.

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya under Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and with Yinshun. He served as a department head at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and taught at Kelaniya.

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who was a research student under C. Kunhan Raja. He was attested as Curator at the Anup Sanskrit Library (1946) and held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1940, 1971).
K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD under M. A. Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. She was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1983.

K. Munirathnam is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy. He served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India, attested between 2013 and 2018.

K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge. He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1954–1963).

K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned an M.A. from Downing College, Cambridge. He served as Lecturer and Reader at the University of Cambridge and edited the Pali Text Society's journal.

K. S. Balasubramanian is an Indology and philosophy scholar affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he was an Editorial Committee member in 2001 and is attested as Director in 2026.

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese was an Indologist and linguist who served as a privaat-docent at Leiden University in 1948 and held a professorship at the University of Amsterdam in 1960.
